messages:
jamal: heads up — after the kernel-fingerprint routing change rolled to canary we saw a ~7% p95 and ~18% p99 increase on host-side tail for short streaming requests (<= 128 tokens). numbers from canary: p50 18ms, p95 62ms (was 58ms), p99 120ms (was 102ms).

maria: any obvious hotspot from the profiler?

jamal: not yet, i ran a quick linux perf on the ingress host and the hot path looks weird — more memcpy calls than before. attaching the sample run.

jamal: ```
$ sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 20
$ sudo perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg
// flame shows big stacks in parse_frame -> coalesce_writev -> memcpy
```

kevin: memcpy spikes usually point to extra copy in the parse/streaming shim. did we change any framing or header parsing when we compute the model kernel fingerprint?

jamal: yeah — kernel-fingerprint now computes a SHA256 over the full request proto to pick a kernel variant. that added an extra bufferization step in the ingress path (we used a temp flattened buffer).

sophie: that explains small writes getting split and then coalesced later — extra copy per message kills tail. can we compute the fingerprint lazily or use a streaming hash?

kevin: streaming hash (incremental) + avoid flattening should be straightforward. code pointer: ingress/route/router.go currently does `proto.Marshal` into []byte before fingerprint. switch to `hash.Write` over the proto fields or use `protoio` stream.

jamal: quick microbench i ran:
```
# before (flatten+sha): 100k req/s, median parse alloc 3.2KB
# after (streaming sha): 118k req/s, median parse alloc 1.1KB
# host p99 tail reduced from 120ms -> 108ms in canary env
```

perf-bot: ALERT: ingress-host parse-copy regression detected in canary (2026-03-19T15:02:01Z). correlates with commit 7f3a2b4 (kernel fingerprint refactor).

maria: can we get a minimal patch for canary rollback vs quick fix? which is lower risk?

kevin: low-risk quick fix = change fingerprint impl to incremental hashing (no external API change). rollback would be heavier since it touches routing choices. i'll open a PR and mark it as hotfix.

jamal: opened PR: #4321 — implements streaming SHA and avoids proto.Marshal. bench in CI confirms perf. tagging @sophie for review.

sophie: glanced at PR, small nits but otherwise LGTM. canary is already trending down after patched nodes rolled. i'll keep watch for the next 24h. :thumbsup:

jamal: action items:
- kevin to land streaming-hash hotfix (inflight)
- maria to watch canary dashboards p95/p99 for next 24h
- if regressions persist, revert commit 7f3a2b4 on canary and do deeper bisect

kevin: starting rollout — will push to remaining canary shards in 10m and report back.

jamal: thanks — if anyone needs the flame.svg i uploaded it to the eng-runtime /perf-assets folder: https://redwood.internal/perf/1789123456-flame.svg

maria: nice find, good triage.
